Q: What is the primary purpose of an access control vestibule (mantrap)?
Option1: Control entry by allowing only one person to pass at a time

Q: What does a badge reader verify?
Option1: Possession of an issued access card
Option4: A one time code from email

Q: What security function does video surveillance provide?
Option1: Monitoring and recording for detection and investigation

Q: Which physical control is designed to detect movement in a protected area?
Option1: Motion sensor

Q: What is the purpose of door locks in physical security?
Option1: Prevent unauthorized access to rooms or cabinets

Q: What do equipment locks protect?
Option1: Individual devices such as laptops or rack equipment

Q: Which control is a human deterrent and responder on site?
Option1: Security guard

Q: What are bollards used for?
Option1: Protect entrances from vehicle impact

Q: What does perimeter fencing primarily provide?
Option1: A physical barrier that deters and delays intruders

Q: Why is security lighting important at building entrances and parking areas?
Option1: It deters intruders and improves camera visibility

Q: What does a magnetometer do in an access control point?
Option1: Detects metallic objects on a person

Q: Which biometric matches blood vessel patterns in the back of the eye?
Option1: Retina scan

Q: Which biometric matches the ridges on a fingertip?
Option1: Fingerprint scan

Q: Which biometric matches friction ridges across the hand surface?
Option1: Palmprint scan

Q: Which item is a proximity device that transmits an identifier when near a reader?
Option1: Key fob

Q: Which physical credential usually contains a chip for contact or contactless verification?
Option1: Smart card

Q: What is the advantage of using traditional keys for some areas?
Option1: Low cost and no electronics required

Q: What is the principle of least privilege?
Option1: Grant only the minimum access required to perform a job
Option2: Grant full access during onboarding then reduce later
Option3: Require two administrators to approve any change
Option4: Deny all access by default permanently

Q: What does an access control list define on a resource?
Option1: Which identities are allowed or denied specific actions
Option2: How to encrypt the data on disk
Option3: The backup schedule for the server
Option4: Which network ports are open on the firewall

Q: What is multifactor authentication?
Option1: Using two or more different factor types to verify identity
Option2: Using two passwords for the same account
Option3: Using two accounts for the same user

Q: Which is an example of a hard token?
Option1: A dedicated hardware key that generates one time codes
Option2: A smartphone app that shows codes
Option3: A code sent by text message

Q: Which is an example of a soft token?
Option1: A one time code generated by an authenticator app
Option2: A hardware key with a display

Q: What is a typical weakness of using short message service codes as a second factor?
Option1: They can be intercepted or redirected
Option3: They work only with smart cards

Q: What describes a voice call based code?
Option1: An automated call reads a one time code to the user
Option2: The user records a passphrase for future comparison
Option3: A voiceprint is matched like a biometric
Option4: A call connects to the help desk for approval

Q: What benefit does an authenticator application provide over SMS?
Option1: Codes are generated locally and do not rely on phone number routing
Option2: It removes the need for passwords

Q: What is the primary purpose of mobile device management in an organization?
Option1: Enforce security policies and manage mobile endpoints

Q: In a Windows domain, what is the purpose of a login script?
Option1: Execute commands or mappings at user sign in

Q: What is a Windows domain used for?
Option1: Centralized authentication and administration of users and computers

Q: What is Group Policy used for?
Option1: Applying standardized configuration and update settings to domain objects

Q: How are organizational units typically used?
Option1: Group users and computers to apply targeted policies and delegation

Q: What does a home folder provide?
Option1: A centrally stored user data location that can follow the user
Option2: A default folder for installing apps
Option3: A hidden folder for caching updates
Option4: A backup of system files only

Q: What is folder redirection used for?
Option1: Store user data on network shares instead of the local profile
Option2: Block users from creating new folders
Option4: Move the entire operating system to a new drive

Q: What do security groups provide in a domain?
Option1: A way to assign permissions to many accounts at once
Option2: A shared mailbox for a team

Q: Which control is primarily preventive?
Option1: Electronic door lock

Q: Which control is primarily detective?
Option1: Security camera monitoring

Q: Which two controls together best reduce tailgating risk at a secure entrance?
Option1: Access control vestibule and security guard

Q: In a scenario where a laptop is frequently used in public spaces, which control best prevents casual theft of the device itself?
Option1: Cable lock attached to a fixed object

Q: A contractor needs temporary building access for one week. Which solution fits best?
Option1: Issue a time limited badge credential
Option3: Provide master keys to all doors

Q: What is the primary purpose of an alarm system in physical security?
Option1: Generate alerts for intrusion or environmental conditions to trigger response

Q: Which statement best describes email one-time codes as a second factor?
Option1: Convenient but weaker; security depends on the mailbox and they are phishable
Option2: As strong as hardware tokens in most cases
Option3: Not permitted by any security frameworks
Option4: They do not work on mobile devices

Q: In a Windows domain, how are operating system update settings commonly enforced?
Option1: Through Group Policy Objects that apply update configurations to targeted organizational units
Option2: By local scripts on each workstation only
Option3: By changing the home folder path
Option4: By creating new security groups with no policies
